sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 04.11.2016 passed by II Additional District and Sessions Court at Bidar, (for short 'tribunal') in MVC.no.733/2015, this appeal is filed.
3.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Court at Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that this appeal was by claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation.
It was submitted that tribunal had assessed compensation and held insurer liable to pay same.

And as insurer had not preferred appeal, finding of tribunal regarding occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to its rash and NC:
2023:KHC-K:6388 negligent driving, claimant sustaining injuries therein leading to amputation of right hand; issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident are not in dispute.

It was submitted that in accident that occurred on 18.06.2005, claimant aged 50 years working as mason and earning `15,000/- per month, sustained amputation of his right hand when driver of Car bearing registration no.MH-24/V-0150 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-56/H-0321, on which claimant was riding and caused accident.

4. It was submitted that though as per medical records namely, injury certificate, discharge summary, discharge card, disability certificate, referral chit, medical bills, reports, prescriptions,
X-ray films etc., produced as Exs.P7, P12 to P20 respectively and deposition of Dr.Sachin as PW-2,
claimant sustained permanent disability of 70% to his right upper limb due to amputation of right hand above elbow, tribunal erred in considering NC: 2023:KHC-K:6388 monthly income of Kashinath S/O Babu Potle vs Rajesh S/O Kashinath Dumne And Anr on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10525459/
2 claimant as `7,500/- and disability at 40%.
It also erred in not adding future prospects.
It was submitted that award towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities, attendant and other incidental charges and laid-up period were grossly inadequate and sought enhancement.
5. On other hand, Shri S.S.Aspalli, learned counsel for respondent no.2 - insurer sought to justify award.
It was submitted that based on material placed before it, tribunal had passed just award and same did not call for interference.

6. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
7.

From above submission, since only claimant is in appeal for enhancement of compensation, point that arises for consideration in this appeal is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6388 8.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimant has stated that he was earning `15,000/- working as mason, no specific evidence was led to substantiate same.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2015 is `8,000/- adopted for purposes of settlement of cases before Lok-Adalat.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
9. As per Ex.P14 - disability certificate, claimant sustained disability of 70% to limb in view of amputation of right hand below shoulder.
Considering, occupation of claimant as mason, loss of right hand (which is usually dominant hand) would lead to substantial disability, if not, total disability.
Considering possibility of other avocation that claimant may be able to perform and earn some livelihood, it would be appropriate to assess loss of earning capacity at 80%.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Erudaya Priya v/s State Express Transport Corporation Limited1, has held that even in injury cases, AIR 2020 SC 4284 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6388 claimant would be entitled for addition of future prospects.

entities.text: Erudaya Priya v/s State Express Transport Corporation Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since disability sustained by claimant is substantial and considering age of claimant as 50 years from medical records, it would be appropriate to add 25% towards future prospects.

Thus, future loss of income would be:
`8,000/- + 25% X 12 X 13 = `15,60,000/-.
10.
Claimant has sustained amputation of his right hand.

Considering his age and occupation, award of `40,000/- towards pain and suffering and `25,000/- towards loss of amenities would be grossly inadequate taking note of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Raj Kumar v/s Ajay Kumar and another2, it would be appropriate to enhance compensation towards pain and suffering to `1,50,000/- and `50,000/- towards loss of amenities.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v/s Ajay Kumar and another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering inpatient period of treatment for eight days, award of `30,000/- towards attendant and other incidental expenses would be justified.

Claimant has sustained amputation, Tribunal (2011) 1 SCC 343 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6388 assessed period of lay-off as four months, since amputation is during treatment, it would be proper to assess period of lay-off for six months.

Thus, claimant would be entitled `48,000/- towards loss Kashinath S/O Babu Potle vs Rajesh S/O Kashinath Dumne And Anr on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10525459/
3 of income during lay-off period.

entities.text: Kashinath S/O Babu Potle vs Rajesh S/O Kashinath Dumne And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As award of `1,82,000/- towards medical expenses being in complete reimbursement of amount for which bills were produced no enhancement is called for.
11.
Amputation of right hand below shoulder would lead to disfigurement of claimant which could be corrected to some extent by use of artificial limb.
It would be appropriate to award sum of `75,000/- towards artificial limb, its periodic maintenance and replacement.
Thus, claimant would be entitled total compensation of `20,95,000/-.
12. This Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Company Limited, Rajasthan vs. Smt.Laxmi and others3 has held rate of interest in motor accident claims cases to be at 6%.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Limited, Rajasthan vs. Smt.Laxmi and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, point for 2018 (4) AKR 808 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6388 consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Accordingly, following :
ORDER Appeal is allowed in part.
Claimant is held entitled for enhanced compensation of `20,95,000/- which shall carry interest at rate of 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
On deposit, insurer is directed to deposit compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Thereafter, Tribunal shall release 40% of enhanced compensation to claimant and keep remaining 60% in any nationalized bank for a period of five years with liberty to draw periodical interest.
